clue.text: Adult in robe, a grotesque thing

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside that other word

blocks.note: a chimer is a loose robe worn by a bishop
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grown-up dressed in a gown, looking like something monstrous.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside CHIMER, and the second A is tacked on the end to give CHIMAERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimaera is a fire-breathing monster of Greek myth, hence any grotesque creature or fantastic figure.

clue.text: Launch hotel with location online

blocks.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a URL is a web address, the location of a page online

explanation.surface: A hotel opening alongside its new website.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch something is to throw or fling it forcefully, which is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: One poem found in friend's home

indicators.note: something found in a word is lodged inside it

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a sonnet is a fourteen-line poem
a mate is a friend; the 's means 'is', so the friend contains the rest

explanation.surface: A poem discovered in a pal's house.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after friend stands for 'is', so the friend is the word that has the rest found in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a self-contained flat on two floors, a type of dwelling, so a kind of home.

clue.text: Last of the substandard glue

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only

blocks.note: final letter of this word
poxy is British slang for worthless or second-rate

explanation.surface: A cheap adhesive dismissed as the worst of a poor lot.
explanation.walkthrough: Poxy is informal British for rubbishy or inferior.
explanation.definitionFit: Epoxy is a resin used as a strong adhesive, so it is a kind of glue.

clue.text: Our team captain's mixed hot water with trifle

definitions.note: a phrase meaning a great fuss over something trivial

indicators.note: mixed letters are stirred together into a new order

blocks.note: all fifteen letters, the 's included

explanation.surface: The skipper made tea from hot water and then served a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Trifle sounds like the custard dessert and hot water like the kettle, but here trifle is a trivial matter and hot water is trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm in a teacup is an idiom for a lot of trouble or anger over a trivial matter.

clue.text: Extravagant — or otherwise — officers

indicators.note: taken the other way round, the little word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
CO is commanding officer, so two officers give CO twice

explanation.surface: A complaint that the commissioned ranks are flamboyant, or perhaps not.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is an ornate eighteenth-century style, and by extension the word means florid or excessively ornamented.

clue.text: Correct clothing is not close to waterproof

indicators.note: a word clothing another wraps around it like a garment

blocks.note: right means correct
ain't is the colloquial contraction of is not

explanation.surface: Proper garments that fall short of keeping you dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not close to' looks like a phrase meaning far from; the definition is 'close to waterproof', and 'is not' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Raintight describes something that keeps out rain without being fully sealed against water, so nearly waterproof.

clue.text: Pass wind when one's left

indicators.note: once the one has departed, that letter is taken out of the word

blocks.note: to wind is to coil
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A schoolboy joke about breaking wind once a companion has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass wind' reads as one phrase, but Pass is the definition and wind is the verb coil.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a high pass or saddle between two mountain peaks, a geography term.

clue.text: Nibbles pieces of meat, swallowing when chopped

indicators.note: something swallowing another takes it inside itself

blocks.note: cuts are joints or portions of meat
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
hewn means cut or chopped

explanation.surface: Someone snacking on diced meat, gulping it down.
explanation.walkthrough: Nibbles looks like a verb, but it is the plural noun for snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashew nuts are a typical party snack, so they are nibbles in the British sense of small things to eat.

clue.text: Cast so, Iron Duke

indicators.note: metal that is cast is poured into a new shape

blocks.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An actor being chosen to play Wellington, the Iron Duke.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Duke was Wellington, but the duke wanted is Orsino, Duke of Illyria in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino is the lovesick Duke of Illyria in Twelfth Night, so a literary duke.

clue.text: Like Manx cat that oddly has "unnamed" ailment

indicators.note: taking a word oddly keeps its first, third and other odd-numbered letters
without a name means the abbreviation for name is dropped

blocks.note: letters one and three
an illness is an ailment

explanation.surface: A Manx cat suffering from some mysterious illness that cannot be named.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name, so ILLNESS loses its N to become ILLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx breed of cat from the Isle of Man is famous for having no tail.

clue.text: Plastic upon leathery moulded material

indicators.note: something plastic can be bent into any shape

blocks.note: all twelve letters

explanation.surface: A description of fake leather made from moulded plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: Plastic looks like the definition but is the anagram signal; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyurethane is a synthetic polymer shaped into foams, coatings and moulded parts, so a moulded material.

clue.text: One toast never translated?

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: one is the indefinite article a
the ten letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinking toast customarily left in its original language.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the French toast is usually said in French, never put into English.
explanation.definitionFit: A votre santé is French for 'to your health', a toast that English speakers commonly use untranslated.

clue.text: Twig below some trees

blocks.note: under means below
a stand is a group of growing trees

explanation.surface: A twig lying underneath a clump of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Twig looks like a noun about a branch; it is the informal verb meaning to grasp or realise.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal British for to catch on or grasp something, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Cleric, scratching head before long

indicators.note: scratching out the head removes the first letter

blocks.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: A clergyman scratching his head, about to say something shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned adverb meaning soon or shortly, as in 'see you anon'.

clue.text: Revive rail company, once buried?

blocks.note: British Rail, the former national railway operator
something buried is in the ground

explanation.surface: A plea to resurrect a defunct railway firm now dead and buried.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail ran Britain's trains until privatisation in the 1990s, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone round is a phrasal verb meaning to restore them to consciousness.

clue.text: Flag down first of taxis and look over it

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
the looking word is spread over the selected letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: blue means sad or down
to peer is to look closely
opening letter

explanation.surface: Hailing a cab and inspecting it before getting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag down' reads as hailing a taxi, but down is a separate word for BLUE. The Blue Peter is a nautical flag signalling a ship is about to sail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Peter is a blue signal flag with a white square, hoisted when a vessel is ready to leave port.

clue.text: Given tranquillity and ambience, books table here?

blocks.note: rest is peace and quiet
an aura is the atmosphere of a place
New Testament, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A diner choosing a place to eat for its calm and atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: Books is also wordplay for NT, and the question mark flags that the definition is playful: a diner books a table there.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant is where people reserve a table to eat, so the place where someone books a table.

clue.text: Babe to have sex with husband

blocks.note: to rut is to mate, of deer in season
abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A sweetheart wanting to sleep with her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Babe sounds like a term of endearment, but it is Babe Ruth, the American baseball star.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe was the nickname of George Herman Ruth, the famous American baseball player.

clue.text: High Church breaks contract for event

indicators.note: a word that breaks into another forces its way inside it

blocks.note: steep means high, as in prices
a lease is a rental contract
abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Catholic congregation reneging on an agreement for a function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Church' reads as one term, but High is STEEP and Church is CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is a horse race or athletics event over jumps and obstacles.

clue.text: Salt's thrown and left in dump

blocks.note: hove is the nautical past tense of heave, so a sailor's word for thrown
abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone tossing salt and leaving it at a rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: A salt is an old sailor, and sailors say hove where others say heaved.
explanation.definitionFit: A dump is informal for a squalid, run-down dwelling, the same idea as a hovel.

clue.text: Surgeon might remove it with skill?

blocks.note: abbreviation for with
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A surgeon operating skilfully to take something out.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the loose definition: a surgeon may excise a skin growth, with skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A wart is a small benign growth on the skin which a doctor can cut away.

clue.text: Derisory quote about right of way

indicators.note: turned about means facing the opposite way, so read backwards

blocks.note: a path is a public right of way
to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at a statement about public access rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisory means so inadequate as to be laughable, which is one sense of pathetic.

clue.text: The meat of white turkey? No

indicators.note: the meat of something is its inner part, so only the central letters are kept

blocks.note: the inner three letters

explanation.surface: A question about whether the white meat is from the turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: A turkey is slang for a flop, so 'turkey? No' means the opposite: a success.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit is a big success, the opposite of a turkey, which is a total failure.

clue.text: New Wave youth turned hooligan

indicators.note: something turned faces the other direction, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a new wave in the arts is its vanguard, van for short
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A punk from the New Wave music scene who went off the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is someone who wilfully damages property, a kind of hooligan.

clue.text: Journalist run over — that's run over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so read backwards

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a tide is something that runs, in or out

explanation.surface: A reporter knocked down by a car, and then knocked down again.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'over' is the reversal signal, so ROTIDE is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a senior journalist who prepares and oversees what a publication prints.

clue.text: Sort of plant pot with metal flaps

indicators.note: something that flaps is flustered and thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener's metal pot with hinged flaps for a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmetto is a fan-leaved palm tree, so a particular kind of plant.
